newsitem.title: NORWAY: Saga to increase exploration off Norway.
newsitem.headline: Saga to increase exploration off Norway.

text.p: Saga Petroleum ASA will spend 700 million crowns ($110.3 million) on exploration drilling on the Norwegian continental shelf in 1997, the company's weekly newsletter said on Monday.
Norway's largest independent oil company said it planned to spud 10 new wells on acreage where it is operator in Norwegian waters and will have five rigs working in the autumn.
But 1998 would be its peak year for exploration with 13 wells planned so far in the 12-month period, it said.

"That figure could go even higher," said Paul Klavenes, vice president for drilling. "We have a number of other interesting prospects for the next four years. The rig portfolio we have secured allows us to drill a maximum of 15 wells per year."

Saga said it would deploy the Bideford Dolphin, which is currently being rebuilt by Aker ASA. It will also use the Scarabeo 5 and Scarabeo 6 from Italy's Saipem, Neddrill Trigon from Dutch Nobel Neddrill and Odfjell's Deepsea Bergen.
"It's about a year since we went to the market to secure this portfolio. We've achieved day rates of $85-105,000. Given the upturn in the market, we're very satisfied with that," said Klavenes.
